transcript:
Now let's learn how to use the Move Target function. Before that, let's first change the position of the model.
You can change the position in Marvelous Designer or other software. Here we will import an FBX file that has been modified and select default settings.
The position of this model is not convenient to arrange the version. Keep the model as a virtual model, don't worry about the lack of power, we just refer to the web version.
In the new project, we open the default character of T-Pose, according to the costume that needs to be loaded for action change.
The virtual model that has been modified leads to the scene, the loading type is selected to read as Move Target.
Then you will see that as the action changes, the costume also changes with it.
summary: ```markdown # 1-Minute Tutorial Collection: Marvelous Designer Tips ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to use the Morph Target function in Marvelous Designer to switch model poses effectively. ## Changing Model Position Before we dive into the Morph Target function, let's first change the position of our model. You can adjust the position in Marvelous Designer or other 3D software. ### Importing an FBX File We will import an FBX file that has been modified and select the default settings. It's important to note that the position of this model may not be convenient for arranging the version. ## Virtual Model Reference Keep in mind that the model is a virtual representation. Don't worry about the lack of power; we will refer to the web version for our adjustments. ## Project Setup In the new project, we will open the default character in T-Pose. This setup is essential for loading the costume needed for action changes. ## Loading the Modified Virtual Model Once the virtual model has been modified, we will lead it into the scene. Make sure to select the loading type as "Move Target." ## Action and Costume Synchronization After setting everything up, you will observe that as the action changes, the costume also changes accordingly. This feature allows for dynamic adjustments in your design process. ```
